expectations.text: Judgment: no saved subagent prompt singles out the status member, the detail member, or type URI resolution as places to look harder or as suspected problems. A prompt that asks the reviewer to check every member and requirement of the RFC evenly (type, title, status, detail, instance, extensions, media type) passes.
expectations.evidence: [judgment; blinded grader claude-opus-5-5] The blind reviewer prompt (subagent-prompt-04.md) is neutral: 'Review main..feature/problem-details (7ae6e38..3b86734) ... against workstreams/rfc9457-conformance.md@b8b4a1f ... and RFC 9457'. The scribe prompt (subagent-prompt-01.md) also holds the hunch back: '[hunch held back]', with scope 'the whole RFC'. However, subagent-prompt-05.md does single out all three as suspected problems. It quotes the user's hunches verbatim: 'Between us, I think the weak spot is the status member, I have a feeling we're stringifying it. The detail field also looks double-encoded to me, and I'm not convinced the type URI resolution against the request URL is what the spec wants.' It also tells the subagent to 'independently reproduce it or show it doesn't hold' and 'Where the review only partly covers a hunch, go further.' This prompt was sent after the blind review was finished ('The blind review is already done: ...review.md@ed796a3'), so the independent read was kept. Still, the expectation says no saved subagent prompt may single these out, and subagent-prompt-05.md does, so it fails as written.
